items.q: I have not filed for two years. Is it too late?
items.a: No. We file the missing returns, work out the penalty and interest, and where there is a reasonable cause we ask the tax office to waive part of it. The sooner you come, the smaller it is.

items.q: Do I need to register for VAT?
items.a: You must once your turnover passes Rs 50 lakh a year for goods, or Rs 30 lakh for services or a mix. Some trades must register from the first rupee. We will check yours.

items.q: Can you work with our billing software?
items.a: Almost certainly. We work with the IRD-approved systems most businesses in Kathmandu use, and with Excel if that is all you have.

items.q: Do I have to come to the office?
items.a: Only for the first meeting, and not even then if you prefer a video call. After that, bills can be sent by photo each week.

props.text: Bring last year’s return and your bank statements. You leave with a written quote.

items.q: Why is the first year sometimes more?
items.a: If the books need rebuilding, we charge for that once, as a catch-up fee agreed in advance. After that, the monthly package is all you pay.

items.q: Do you charge for phone calls?
items.a: No. Call or message as often as you like.

items.q: Do you give discounts to new businesses?

pages.title: Tax calendar
pages.seoTitle: Nepal tax calendar: VAT, TDS, advance tax and income tax dates
pages.seoDescription: The Nepali fiscal year month by month: VAT and TDS by the 25th, advance tax in Poush, Chaitra and Asar, income tax returns by the end of Asoj.

props.title: The dates that matter, in the Nepali calendar
props.text: The fiscal year runs from 1 Shrawan to the end of Asar. These are the deadlines most small businesses face. Your own may differ; ask us.

primary.label: Get a reminder before each one

items.title: VAT return and TDS
items.text: For the previous Nepali month. Filed online, paid by bank or wallet.

items.title: New fiscal year
items.text: Close last year’s books, count stock, renew registrations that expire.

items.title: Income tax return
items.text: For the year that ended in Asar. An extension of up to three months can be requested in writing.

items.title: First advance tax instalment
items.text: 40% of the estimated tax for this year. Also the extended deadline for last year’s return.

items.title: Second advance tax instalment
items.text: Paid up to 70% of the estimate.

items.title: Final instalment and year end
items.text: The remaining 30%. Count stock on the last day.

image.alt: A calculator, reading glasses, printed charts and binders on a desk

props.caption: The week before Asoj ends, our office stays open until seven.

items.title: The VAT threshold
items.text: Registration is required above Rs 50 lakh a year in goods, or Rs 30 lakh in services or a mix.

items.title: Late VAT returns
items.text: Carry a fee and interest on unpaid tax, even when no tax is due. File a nil return if you had no sales.

items.title: Rent and TDS
items.text: Rent paid by a business usually needs tax deducted at source and deposited by the 25th.

items.title: Cash payments
items.text: Large cash payments may not be accepted as business expenses. Pay suppliers through the bank.

props.heading: A reminder three days before each deadline
